#### 0. Loading Necessary Packages 
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(rvest)
library(purrr)

set.seed(1)
```

#### Problem 1. 
```{r}

bday = function(n) {
  bdays = sample.int(365, size = n, replace = TRUE)
  dup = length(unique(bdays)) < n
  
  return(dup)
}

bday_results_df = 
  expand_grid(
    n = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |>
  mutate(
    duplicate = map_lgl(n, bday)
  ) |>
  group_by(n) |>
  summarize(
    prob = mean(duplicate)
  )

bday_results_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = prob)) + 
  geom_line()
    
```

Probability that at least two people in a group with share the same birthday increases as group size increases. There are steep increases in probability between n = 10 and around n = 30. The probability of a duplicate birthday crosses the 50% mark when the group size is  `r bday_results_df |> filter(prob > 0.50) |> pull(n) |> min()` These steep increases start to flatten as group size approaches n = 50. When the group size is 50 individuals, the probability simulated is close to 100, at around `r bday_results_df |> filter(n==50) |> pull(prob) * 100`%.
